title: New ‘First Proof’ exam reveals how AI-powered math is a pay-to-play sport
key_facts: The First Proof project, started in February by top mathematicians, released its third batch of results on 14 Oct 2026.
Ten research problems were chosen; each model answered with no human input and three graders per problem reviewed the answers.
The best performer, ProofCouncil (a combination built on OpenAI's GPT 6 Astra), solved nine of 10 to a 'minor revisions' standard.
Round one's top model solved a few problems; round two's winner solved six or seven.
The best open-weight model, Kimi K3, solved none.
OpenAI's newest internal model was excluded because entrants must be openly available; Google did not take part.
Mohammed Abouzaid of Stanford says the gap between open-weight and frontier models is very large in research maths.
quote_evidence: “The gap between the open-weight models and frontier models is very large in research mathematics—much larger than in other domains,”
Notably, the best open-weight model, Kimi K3, solved exactly zero problems.
why_it_matters_hint: Independent test shows frontier AI nearly solves research-level proofs while open models fall far behind.
